content:
I want to write this message mostly to record an issue that I have encountered in how we tag mathlib commits. The current situation is that the most up-to-date stable version of Lean is 4.29.1, but the most recent tag that exists in mathlib that corresponds to a stable toolchain is 4.29.0. If you use lake new foo math, it will (probably) fail since it tries to set up a new project foo with the most recent stable version of lean, and tries to tie the mathlib ref to the associated tag.

Let's have a discussion on how to fix this. Tagging the relevant people: @Kim Morrison @Anne Baanen @Bryan Gin-ge Chen (any others?)

Indeed, lake new foo math does fail:

$ lake new foo math
info: foo: no previous manifest, creating one from scratch
info: leanprover-community/mathlib: cloning https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4
error: foo/.lake/packages/mathlib: revision not found 'v4.29.1'

I haven't looked much at the tagging scripts / workflows before. Happy to coordinate with Kim and / or anyone else to improve things here.

A related issue I'd like to bring up again is how the tagged commits work with docgen and specifically docgen-action. I find it confusing how the tag for docgen will sometimes lag behind the tag for Mathlib, then downstream projects that update quickly will have an unexpected failure building docs via the GitHub action. (Which I guess doesn't affect Mathlib because the documentation build is customized).
I think we've discussed this before; lake new foo math should be fetching mathlib first to determine which lean version to use, not fetching lean and hoping that a mathlib release is ready
(of course we should also create the tags whenever possible, but we need the above if we want to avoid race conditions)
@Joscha Mennicken Maybe you might be a good person to tag here: should we (set up automation to) create new commits for new tagged releases of Lean 4? Happy to assist in any way I can here.
I tried to tag a v4.29.1 but CI didn't like it: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/tree/bump_to_v4.29.1

Chris Henson said:

A related issue I'd like to bring up again is how the tagged commits work with docgen and specifically docgen-action. I find it confusing how the tag for docgen will sometimes lag behind the tag for Mathlib, then downstream projects that update quickly will have an unexpected failure building docs via the GitHub action. (Which I guess doesn't affect Mathlib because the documentation build is customized).

I've updated the release procedure to reduce the time it takes until doc-gen4 is updated, which means that it should usually be updated before mathlib.

Joscha Mennicken said:

I tried to tag a v4.29.1 but CI didn't like it: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/tree/bump_to_v4.29.1

Aha, the issue is that the version of cache used in the master branch is not compatible with older toolchains. I've gone ahead and copied branch#bump_to_v4.28.1 and branch#bump_to_v4.29.1 to branch#ci-dev/bump_to_v4.28.1 and branch#ci-dev/bump_to_v4.29.1 so that we can run CI on them manually with their own tool chains here: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/workflows/ci_dev.yml

Assuming the following are green we can then create the v4.28.1 and v4.29.1 tags, right?

  • CI for ci-dev/bump_to_v4.28.1
  • CI for ci-dev/bump_to_v4.29.1
Yes, that sounds right, though we should probably test lake exe cache get before tagging. Thanks for your efforts!

OK, I've pushed the v4.28.1 and v4.29.1 tags and I've confirmed that lake new foo math now works.

A v4.29.1 release was also automatically created and it looks like the release for v4.28.1 was created manually yesterday.

I did a quick comparison of the tags in the lean4 and mathlib4 repos and it looks like the only discrepancies are for some rc releases so I think we're good for the time being.

Last question: I think I understand the process now, but do we want any additional automation for this in mathlib4?
No, I don't think so. I'd consider this part of the release process, and those scripts and docs live in the lean4 repo.

@Joscha Mennicken I just noticed that branch#stable is still pointing to a commit where the toolchain is v4.29.0, should it be updated?

Also, since I've always been curious, what are the "rules" for stable and how is it intended to be used?

edit: Ah, I guess on the tags and branches community page there's a comment in the batteries section which probably applies here as well:

There is a branch stable which follows the v4.X.0 tags.

I guess my question is then whether that should be v4.X.Y instead?

I'm not sure, but I think it would make sense to bump the stable branch? Though I'm also not quite sure about how v4.X.1 patch releases affect the ecosystem since all packages involved in the release process fervently follow the latest release candidates.
Yes, I think that is a mistake, and stable should follow v4.X.Y (and this should be the norm for all projects using toolchain version tags and a stable branch).
I just remembered this thread and have bumped stable to v4.29.1.
Should that become a step in some release script?
@Joscha Mennicken has recently replaced many of my scripts with saner replacements. I'm not sure if this is something that fell through the gaps, or just never worked properly.
v4.X.1 stable releases when a v4.(X+1).0-rcY is already out are quite different from normal releases, so I did this one by hand and forgot a few things, sorry.
